sections.h2: Which Lawrence County offices deal with a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Four offices in Louisa handle the tax year between them, and the PVA and the sheriff list the same Main Cross Street address. Each one covers a different stage.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): 122 Main Cross Street, Louisa, KY 41230. The PVA sets the assessed value and takes homestead applications.
  • Sheriff: 122 Main Cross Street, Louisa. Phone (606) 638-4368. The sheriff takes payment.
  • County Clerk: runs the appeals board paperwork and, after April, the sale of unpaid bills. The clerk's site posts the current delinquent list.
  • County Attorney: mails the warning letters to owners whose bills have moved to the clerk.

Rates differ from one taxing district to the next, so take the bill from the sheriff and the assessed value from the PVA for your own parcel.

sections.h2: What is Lawrence County like for a property owner?
sections.html:
Lawrence County was formed in 1821 from parts of Floyd and Greenup counties and has had four courthouses over the years. Louisa is the county seat and the only city. In the east, a quarter-mile concrete T-bridge links Louisa to Fort Gay, West Virginia, across the point where the Levisa Fork and the Tug River join to form the Big Sandy River. Yatesville Lake, a reservoir of about 2,300 acres opened in 1992 and managed by the Army Corps of Engineers, provides flood control and recreation. Alcohol sales are limited to Louisa city limits.

  • People: an estimated 15,765 in July 2025, compared with 16,293 counted in 2020 and 15,860 in 2010. About 416 square miles of land works out to 39 residents per square mile.
  • Housing: 7,737 units and 6,342 households, with 77.8 percent owned by their occupants.
  • Middle home value: $111,700. Monthly owner costs have a median of $1,216 with a mortgage and $386 without one, and median rent is $760.
  • Income: $46,772 for the median household, with 23.4 percent of people in poverty.
  • Work: 207 employer establishments with 2,950 jobs in 2023, a 5.9 percent rise over 2022, and a 30.1 minute average commute.
  • Connectivity and school: 83.7 percent of households have broadband, and 81.7 percent of adults 25 and older finished high school.

sections.h2: When is a Lawrence County tax bill due, and what does lateness cost?
sections.html:
Under KRS 134.015 the sheriff wants the money by December 31, and owners who pay everything by November 1 keep 2 percent. The penalty is 5 percent during January and 10 percent from then on. The state's sample for a $1,000 bill makes the late cost concrete: a $100 penalty plus a $110 sheriff add-on fee, so the bill is about 21 percent higher from February 1, before any commission.

If bills go out after November 1, the state applies an alternative schedule with 30 days for each stage. Oil and gas bills also exist in Lawrence County. The clerk's delinquent tax page says its sale leaves out the 2023 oil and gas bills, so ask the sheriff whether one is attached to your parcel.

sections.h2: What is the appeal route for a Lawrence County assessment?
sections.html:
The sequence runs in order. The owner meets the PVA or a deputy, looks at the roll during its May viewing window, files with the county clerk the next workday after viewing closes, and then argues the case before the local board of assessment appeals about a month later. The board hears evidence only, so bring descriptions of the land and buildings, insurance papers, building costs and sales of similar houses.

Written reasons follow any change the board makes. Hearings may be recorded, and a paid representative has to fit the categories in KRS 133.120. Skipping the board closes off the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: Which Lawrence County owners can claim the homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Owners at least 65 years old and owners classified as totally disabled qualify. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the exemption lowers the assessment by $49,100, which turns a $150,000 assessment into $100,900 for tax purposes. Lawrence County has an older population, with 19.9 percent aged 65 or more, and 17.5 percent of residents under 65 report a disability.

File with the PVA in the courthouse. Disability claims need yearly renewal, apart from veterans with a service connected disability and owners ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or the state retirement systems.

sections.h2: How does the Lawrence County Clerk sell unpaid tax bills?
sections.html:
After the sheriff's April 15 cutoff, unpaid bills go to the clerk as certificates of delinquency, and interest of 1 percent a month starts. The county attorney mails notices, and the clerk advertises the list before the sale. At the sale a third party can buy the lien, and the owner then pays that buyer instead. The Lawrence County Clerk's website lays out how its draft-style sale works, which also tells an owner how much the buyer may be paying.

Lawrence County Clerk delinquent tax sale rules (lawrencekyclerk.com, delinquent taxes page)
ItemRule
RegistrationAt least 10 business days before the sale
Deposit$10 per bill, capped at $250, not refundable
Prior year certificatesSeparate list due 10 business days before the sale
Bidders per entityOne potential purchaser
Order of purchaseRandom drawing, lowest number picks first, in rounds
PaymentCash, certified check, money order or company check
RefundsNone after the sale

The lien on the land from delinquent taxes lasts eleven years under KRS 134.015, no matter who owns the property.

sections.h2: What should a Lawrence County seller handle before listing?
sections.html:
• Ask the sheriff at (606) 638-4368 for the current bill and any earlier unpaid year.
  • Check the clerk's delinquent list to see whether a certificate already exists on the parcel.
  • If you hold the homestead exemption, ask the PVA how it is treated after a sale.
  • Compare your assessment with the sales of similar houses before the May inspection window opens, in case a dispute is worth filing.
  • Agree on the split of the current bill in the sales contract.

A seller who would rather not repair or show the house can ask for a direct offer. Taxes still come out of the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Lawrence County?
faqs.a: The Lawrence County Sheriff collects it at 122 Main Cross Street in Louisa. Call (606) 638-4368 to confirm the amount and the payment methods before you go.

faqs.q: What is the early payment discount in Lawrence County?
faqs.a: Two percent, if the bill is paid in full by November 1. KRS 134.015 sets that discount, and the printed amount applies from November 2 through December 31.

faqs.q: What is the first step to dispute a Lawrence County assessment?
faqs.a: Meet with the PVA or a deputy. The local board of assessment appeals will not hear an owner who has not had that conference first.

faqs.q: How much does the homestead exemption remove from the assessment?
faqs.a: It removes $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Owners must be 65 or older or classified as totally disabled, and the PVA takes the application.

faqs.q: Can a third party buy my unpaid Lawrence County tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. If a certificate of delinquency is unpaid at the clerk's sale, a registered third party purchaser can buy the lien, and the owner then pays that buyer.
